expected_effect: Direction: lower public_val_bpb via more optimizer steps in the fixed 1800 s budget with unchanged per-step math. Predeclared size: +2% to +5% complete steps vs same-host control (2112-2175 trn21; 2118-2180 trn22) and public_val_bpb lower by 0.001-0.003 (SUCCESS requires >= +2% steps and >= 0.001 lower BPB; steps within +/-1% is FALSIFIED-INERT; >= +2% steps with BPB >= control is FALSIFIED-QUALITY; +1..2% steps or a positive gain < 0.001 is INCONCLUSIVE). Smoke prediction: >= 340 steps on either host (control 334/335) and public_val_bpb <= control smoke + 0.003.
hypothesis: In the pinned control every rank redundantly executes the compiled Muon Newton-Schulz (NS) orthogonalization for every matrix of every same-shape batch (MuonAdamW._muon_step -> fn from _MUON_COMPILED, i.e. torch.compile(_muon_math, backend='neuron', dynamic=False)). NS is the only super-linear part of the optimizer (BF16 matmul chain on g.bfloat16() per iteration) and it is replicated 4x across the LNC=2 nproc=4 ranks. Partitioning only the NS stage by contiguous ownership and reconstructing the full orthogonalized batch with one all_gather removes ~3/4 of that work per rank at the cost of one small BF16 collective per shape group. fs-w65 measured this exact mechanism at +5.06245% complete steps after an exact numerical gate on a 117.5M dense model; fs-w70/w98/w146 retained it. Because train.py schedules by elapsed time, more steps in 1800 s should lower fixed-budget public_val_bpb, as the bf16-sdpa-input row did (2233 vs 2076 steps -> 1.002028 vs 1.005967).
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-muon-owner-ns-split-r4 from 9a4caa7b. Read-only reference (adapt names, do not copy verbatim): research/scratch/fresh_start_train.py --experimental-optimizer-ownership path at the same commit. STEP 1 (static inspection, reported only as a note inside the implementation summary; no artifact file, no execution): open class MuonAdamW; locate step() (calls _muon_step once per same-shape group), _muon_step, its backend dispatch (the compiled branch that looks up fn in _MUON_COMPILED, created via torch.compile(_muon_math, backend='neuron', dynamic=False), versus the eager/NKI branch), and the module-level _muon_math. Record _muon_math's full parameter list. Inside _muon_math identify three contiguous statement groups and quote their line ranges: (a) PRE = every statement up to and including the g.bfloat16() cast that produces the NS input (out-of-place torch.lerp momentum update, Nesterov blend, cast); note the updated momentum buffer is a RETURN value that _muon_step rebinds. (b) NS = the NS-input normalization statement(s) plus both Newton-Schulz loops through the last iteration; note that these statements read tall and ns_steps. (c) POST = every statement after NS (shape-dependent scale if present, second-moment update/normalization, LR/weight-decay scaling, parameter update, construction of the return tuple). Confirm every rank runs (b) for every matrix in the compiled branch; if it is already split by rank followed by a collective, stop and report HALT-INERT. Also record how main() selects the compiled branch and its precedence over --nki-muon; do not change that selection. STEP 2 (toggle): following the existing --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add module-level USE_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE = True with env override NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE ('0' disables), argparse pair --muon-owner-compute / --no-muon-owner-compute (dest muon_owner_compute, default None -> constant), resolved in main() before the optimizer is constructed. Do NOT add it to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES (it does not affect forward, weights, checkpoints or evaluation). STEP 3 (extraction by moving statements, no rewriting; _muon_math itself stays byte-for-byte unchanged and _MUON_COMPILED stays unchanged): add three module-level functions next to _muon_math. _muon_pre(<exactly the subset of _muon_math's parameters read by group (a)>) contains the group (a) statements and returns (new_momentum, G) where G is the BF16 NS input of shape [n, *shape]; semantics stay out-of-place (no in-place momentum update is introduced). _muon_ns(X, tall, ns_steps) contains exactly the group (b) statements operating on a stacked batch X of arbitrary leading size, with tall and ns_steps passed explicitly (same specialization and iteration count as _muon_math), returning the orthogonalized batch in the same dtype _muon_math has at that point. _muon_post(orth, <exactly the subset of _muon_math's parameters read by group (c), plus the new momentum where the return tuple includes it>) contains exactly the group (c) statements and returns exactly the tensors _muon_math returns, in the same order. Compile each helper with the identical treatment: torch.compile(<helper>, backend='neuron', dynamic=False), cached in three new module-level dicts _MUON_PRE_COMPILED, _MUON_NS_COMPILED, _MUON_POST_COMPILED keyed exactly as _MUON_COMPILED is keyed (for _MUON_NS_COMPILED additionally include the leading batch size so the [per_rank, *shape] and [n, *shape] variants are separate entries). STEP 4 (partition, compiled branch only): inside the existing compiled branch of _muon_step, before the current fn(...) call, compute owner_active = USE_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE and torch.distributed.is_available() and torch.distributed.is_initialized() and torch.distributed.get_world_size() > 1 and n >= 2. If not owner_active, execute the existing fn(...) call and rebinding exactly as today. Otherwise: (i) new_mom, G = compiled _muon_pre(...) and rebind the momentum state exactly where _muon_step rebinds the _muon_math return today; (ii) world_size = get_world_size(), rank = get_rank(); per_rank = (n + world_size - 1) // world_size; start = rank * per_rank; owned = G[start:min(start + per_rank, n)]; if owned.shape[0] < per_rank, local_stack = torch.cat([owned] + [G[0:1]] * (per_rank - owned.shape[0]), dim=0), else local_stack = owned (copies of matrix 0, never zeros, so no normalization guard changes; padded outputs are discarded); (iii) local_out = compiled _muon_ns(local_stack, tall, ns_steps); (iv) gathered = [torch.empty_like(local_out) for _ in range(world_size)]; torch.distributed.all_gather(gathered, local_out) on the default process group, executed in ordinary (lazy-XLA) code outside any compiled region; full_out = torch.cat(gathered, dim=0)[:n] (rank-order concatenation, so index k of full_out is matrix k of the batch under the contiguous mapping); (v) results = compiled _muon_post(full_out, ...) and rebind/apply exactly as _muon_step does with fn's return today. The eager/NKI branch of _muon_step is not modified in any way. Do not change parameter iteration order, state tensors, gradient all-reduce, clipping, --clip-after-reduce/--grad-bucket logic, AdamW/ngram-ve optimizers, schedules, model, data or evaluation code. STEP 5 (once-per-group equivalence check, diagnostics only, executes at smoke runtime): keep a module-level dict _MUON_OWNER_CHECKED keyed by (tuple(shape), n). On the first owner_active _muon_step call for a key: before STEP 4 (i), clone every tensor argument the existing compiled fn call would receive (parameters, gradients, momentum, second-moment state) and record param_before = clone of the parameters; run ref = fn(*cloned_args) using the SAME control callable from _MUON_COMPILED (not eager _muon_math) so the reference is exactly the pinned control's compiled arithmetic; collect ref_params (returned or in-place-updated clones), ref_mom, ref_sm. Also compute ref_ns = compiled _muon_ns(G, tall, ns_steps) on the full batch after (i). After STEP 4 (v), compute: ns_rel = (full_out.float() - ref_ns.float()).abs().max() / ref_ns.float().abs().max().clamp_min(1e-30); delta_rel = ((cand_param - param_before) - (ref_param - param_before)).abs().max() / (ref_param - param_before).abs().max().clamp_min(1e-30) (max over the group's parameters); mom_rel and sm_rel analogously as max_abs_diff / max_abs_ref over momentum and second-moment state. Print on rank 0 one line: 'muon_owner_check shape=<tuple> n=<n> per_rank=<k> ns_rel=<f> delta_rel=<f> mom_rel=<f> sm_rel=<f>' (a handful of .item() syncs once per group). The real update always uses the split-path results; clones and references are discarded; mark the key checked. STEP 6 (logging): add exactly one field 'muon_owner_compute=<bool>' to the existing optimizer/sched_tricks config oneliner printed at startup; if the compiled branch is not the selected backend, print one line 'muon_owner_compute: inactive (non-compiled NS backend)' at startup. STEP 7 (static self-review inside the implementation summary; no execution required): state that the diff is limited to the toggle/env/CLI resolution, the three moved-statement helpers and their caches, the owner_active block inside the compiled branch of _muon_step, the once-per-group check, and the log field; state that _muon_math, _MUON_COMPILED and the eager/NKI branch are unchanged and that the unchanged compiled fn runs when the toggle is off, world_size == 1 or n < 2; state that forward/eval code, ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES, checkpoint format and optimizer state tensors are unchanged; quote the group (a)/(b)/(c) line ranges. Runtime verification (muon_owner_check tolerances, step-rate, BPB, causality) belongs to the Operator's smoke run per the abort conditions. Launch smoke and full with the exact control launch command and environment (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 train.py --num-steps 5000 --max-train-seconds 1800 --seed 42; NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1) and no additional flags.
single_causal_change: One optimizer-implementation change confined to train.py, inserted ONLY inside the existing compiled branch of MuonAdamW._muon_step (the branch that fetches fn from _MUON_COMPILED); the eager and NKI branches and main()'s existing compile-muon-over-nki-muon backend precedence are untouched. When the new module-level toggle USE_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE is on (default True; env NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE='0' disables; CLI --muon-owner-compute/--no-muon-owner-compute), torch.distributed is initialized with world_size > 1, and the batch has n >= 2 matrices, the compiled branch runs the SAME arithmetic as _muon_math split at the NS stage into three identically compiled helpers: (pre) out-of-place momentum/Nesterov statements and the g.bfloat16() NS-input cast on every rank, returning the new momentum buffer (rebound exactly as today) and the BF16 NS input G; (ns) the NS-input normalization plus both NS loops, moved verbatim and taking tall and ns_steps as explicit arguments, executed on every rank only for its contiguous owned slice (rank r owns [r*per_rank, min((r+1)*per_rank, n)), per_rank = ceil(n/world_size); local stack has static shape [per_rank, *shape]; unowned slots are filled with copies of G[0:1] and discarded), followed by ONE torch.distributed all_gather that reconstructs the full orthogonalized batch in rank order sliced to n; (post) the remaining statements (shape-dependent scale, second-moment update/normalization, LR/weight-decay scaling, parameter update, return tuple) on every rank on the reconstructed batch, returning exactly what _muon_math returns in the same order. When the toggle is off, world_size == 1, n < 2, or the compiled branch is not the selected backend, the unchanged _MUON_COMPILED fn executes as today. Momentum/second-moment layout, optimizer state and checkpoint format, gradient all-reduce, clipping, AdamW/ngram-ve optimizers, schedules, model, forward/eval code, data, seed, evaluator, launch shape and environment are unchanged. Full-run classification vs the same-host pinned control (trn21 2071/1.005734; trn22 2076/1.005967), evaluated in order: (1) HALT-INERT if static inspection finds NS already partitioned across ranks in the compiled branch (no patch, no run); (2) HALT-NUMERICS if the smoke log lacks a 'muon_owner_check' line for any partitioned (shape, n) group, or any such line reports ns_rel > 1.5625e-2 (2 BF16 ulps; the NS chain is BF16), delta_rel > 3.125e-2, mom_rel > 1e-5, sm_rel > 1e-3, or a non-finite value, or smoke public_val_bpb > same-host control smoke (1.165855 trn21 / 1.165604 trn22) + 0.003, or smoke causality_passed is False; (3) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if full-run steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (4) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control; (5) SUCCESS if steps >= +2% of control and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.001; (6) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control; (7) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (including +1..2% steps, or >= +2% steps with a positive gain smaller than 0.001). If steps exceed +10% (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22) the verdict is still assigned by (5)-(7) on the fixed-budget public_val_bpb; the Analyst additionally records the muon_owner_check lines and the smoothed training-loss log value at the control's final step count as attribution notes only (not validation BPB; they do not alter the verdict).
